card st-run-start-guard  [decided]
The start of a run refuses while a run is in progress on its subtree or an ancestor
why: An agent starts runs from the command line, not from a button. If only the board disabled the start, an agent could still start a second run, and two runs would write overlapping tickets and build against the same code. So the rule sits where every run starts, and the board only shows what it refuses.

A run is **in progress** when its process is alive (see #vi-board-state). Every way to start a run checks the same rule before it starts: a run in progress on the same subtree, or on any ancestor of it, makes the start fail. The refusal names the blocking run and where to find it. The same refusal holds for a resume, a restart and a plan over that subtree. The board shows the same fact as a disabled control (see #vi-board-plan-controls).

A restart ends the unfinished work of a subtree first (see #werk-board-restart). The command line has its own restart. It must say that it ends the unfinished work, and it prints each running build it cancels and each ticket it archives, so an agent cannot restart by accident. A run on a descendant of the subtree is not covered by this rule.

Example:

- Billing "Billing" is the parent of X "Invoices".
- A run is in progress on Billing.
- An agent starts a run on X from the command line.

1. The start is refused. The message says "a run is in progress on Billing" and points to its plan card. Nothing starts, and nothing is written to X.
2. The run on Billing ends.
3. The agent starts the run on X again. It starts. X has no unfinished work, so a new plan and run begin.
4. The agent starts the run on X once more while it is in progress. The start is refused: a run is in progress on X.
5. The run on X stops, and 3 unfinished tickets stay. The agent asks to restart. The command line prints "ends the unfinished work: cancel the build of 3, archive 3, 4 and 5" and waits for the agent to say it means it.

```
 start run on X
      |
      v
 run in progress on X or on an ancestor?
      |                         |
     yes                        no
      v                         v
 refused: names the        unfinished work on X?
 blocking run                |            |
                            yes           no
                             v            v
                   resume, or a confirmed   plan, then run
                   restart that lists
                   what it ends
```

card st-build-steps  [decided]
Build: a builder loop per ticket and a merge loop per run
why: One ticket is built alone in its own worktree. A run merges many tickets into one tree. The two need different loops with different stop conditions.
subtree: 44 cards, 1 open, 43 decided

Build turns a decided subtree into merged, checked code. It runs on two levels: a builder loop for each ticket in its own worktree (#st-build-ticket), and a merge loop over the finished tickets of a run (#st-build-run).

**Words.** The per-ticket step is "check", not "validate". Validate
node src/cli.ts show st-build-run-mechanics | head -30; node src/cli.ts help 2>&1 | grep -iE "move|reparent|parent"

card st-build-run-mechanics  [decided]
The merge loop drives one run: a temporary merge worktree, a guarded branch move, and a stop when a build stays red
why: The merge loop has to be safe to resume and must never overwrite a run tree that moved under it.
subtree: 2 cards, 2 decided

- Starting the merge loop on a planned subtree is the person's trigger for its tickets. Starting it again resumes.
- The merge queue merges the ticket's branch in a detached worktree and runs the ticket's own checks there.
- The main line moves only from the value it had when the merge started, so a main line that changed in between is never overwritten (#st-plan-main). A checkout of the main line moves with it by a fast-forward. A checkout whose local changes block that fast-forward stops the loop, and nothing moves.
- After a red merge, the next build starts from the ticket's old branch when that branch sits on top of the main line.
- A ticket's retry cap counts passes across all its builds, so it also bounds the trips between the builder and the merge queue.
- A build that stays red stops the loop as stuck.
- Every start of the loop writes the feature tier event to the board log first (#werk-loop-tier).
- G2 belongs to the main line's tip: a later merge opens it again. Only a person passes it (#st-gates).

I moved #st-run-start-guard. It now sits directly under #st-build-steps, and no stale mark came out of the move.

You were right about where it belongs. #st-build-run-mechanics covers how one merge loop works inside. The guard is a rule between runs. It holds for every start, resume, restart and plan, so it sits next to #st-build-died and #st-build-target.

Its dependencies on #werk-board-restart and #vi-board-state did not change.
